domain: Jurilinguistics and multilingual legal drafting - equally authentic texts, co-drafting and revision, concordance of defined terms, recitals versus operative provisions, testing clauses, and Vienna Convention Art. 33 divergence
axioms: When one meaning is written twice, the two writings drift; the only question is which one governs and who discovers the divergence first.
A text is read alone. The party consulting one language never sees the other, so a defect is invisible at the point of drafting and total at the point of use.
Revision is line-by-line against the source text, never against memory or a paraphrase of it; a summary of the original cannot be revised against.
A defined term is defined once and cross-referenced thereafter; restating it in a second place creates two definitions and no rule for which prevails.
A promise made in a recital binds nothing; only the operative provision does the work, so every recital must be traced to the article that delivers it.
An instruction is addressed to an official with no local knowledge, and is defective if it requires anything not on the page.
A testing or enacting clause that the official cannot satisfy as written means the instrument does not come into force, however sound its substance.
primitives: authentic text (each independent implementation of one meaning: graph.py / graph.js, thresholds.py / constants.js, embedding_text in either language)
defined term (a result-shape key or field name that a downstream reader dereferences)
concordance entry (one row of the 17-name export table, paired with its actual call site)
operative provision (a numbered step an executor will perform literally)
recital (a Must-Have, Key Link, or folded-finding claim that asserts rather than instructs)
testing clause (a <verify> line, judged on whether it is satisfiable as written)
divergence (a specific, quotable pair of statements that no longer say the same thing)
mandate gap (knowledge a step assumes that the text does not carry)
failure_mode: Blind to anything stated only once and correctly: a single-source risk with no parallel text produces no signal at all.
Treats runtime, performance, security and operational exposure as outside the instrument - a text that is coherent, executable and disastrous reads as clean.
Cannot judge whether a duplicated statement matters in practice; over-reports harmless redundancy (a constant repeated in a comment) alongside load-bearing drift.
Reads only what is written, so a defect that lives in the machines, the network or the data - never in the text - is systematically missed.
Weak on emergent, cross-task behaviour and timing; the domain has no concept of two officials acting concurrently, only of two texts disagreeing.
Anchors on the plan and the code in this worktree, and will not go get external state (npm, GitHub, another machine) to settle whether a divergence is real.
